purpose: Before selecting the next V4 performance target, identify which primitives and partner routes already existed in V2.14 for each benchmark app. This prevents V4 from counting front-door migration or partner/productization work as a new V4 speed win.

summary.existing_app_selection_rule: An existing benchmark app can support a new V4 performance claim only if V4 either introduces a generic primitive/runtime lever absent in V2.14, or proves the same primitive is materially faster than the V2.14 app route under the frozen same-hardware app protocol. Otherwise it is productization or parity, not a V4 speed win.
summary.next_goal4672_effect: Do not finalize robot_collision as the next target until its denominator is explicitly framed as same-primitive improvement over V2.14. Prefer a target whose needed lever is not already a V2.14 promoted primitive, or declare that a new generic primitive must be built.

apps.v2_14_primary_route: RTDL/OptiX active-frontier nearest-witness plus generic grouped max continuation

v2_14_measured_goal4669_route.note: The Goal4669 V2.14 denominator row used Embree directed-summary style evidence, while the V2.14 route table also records an OptiX nearest-witness primitive-first path.

apps.v4_implication: V4 Hausdorff improvements must be framed as official-route/productized continuation and measured app-route improvement, not as first invention of nearest-witness primitives.

apps.v2_14_primary_route: mixed explicit RayJoin route from Goal4039 RTX 4000 Ada fixed-Numba-toolchain evidence
apps.v2_14_primitive_contract: prepared point/closed-shape batch count, segment-pair exact count, shape-pair active count
apps.v4_implication: Current V4 has no app route for spatial_rayjoin. A future V4 win would require a new generic relation-topology route, not reuse of the old mixed Numba/OptiX evidence.

apps.v2_14_primary_route: mixed explicit RT-DBSCAN route with grouped-stream Numba/CuPy and explicit direct-status variants
apps.v2_14_primitive_contract: fixed-radius count-threshold device columns plus grouped stream component labels
apps.v4_implication: Goal4670/4671 modest results are expected: V2.14 already had the count-threshold plus grouped-union primitive path. V4 needs a genuinely new grouped-union lever or must stop treating RTDBSCAN as a second-win target.

apps.v2_14_primitive_contract: prepared any-hit collision flag and scalar count
apps.v4_implication: Robot collision is not a clean second true V4 win target by default, because V2.14 already exposed prepared OptiX any-hit collision flags including device-buffer modes. It may only be selected as a same-primitive improvement experiment with V2.14 as the explicit denominator.
A V4 win would require a new generic full contact-manifold route or materially faster bounded collect-k path, not just reusing the V2.14 bounded witness primitive.
V4 grouped-i64 catalog work mostly productizes and bounds an existing V2.14 primitive-first path. It cannot by itself prove V4 is faster than V2.14.

apps.v2_14_primary_route: RTDL/OptiX membership primitive plus explicit force-vector partner continuation
apps.v2_14_primitive_contract: aggregate-frontier membership plus grouped vector continuation
apps.v4_implication: Barnes-Hut remains one of the few places where a true V4 path could exist if a generic fused aggregate-tree weighted-vector primitive beats the V2.14 membership-plus-partner route. That must be proven as generic pushdown, not Barnes-Hut app identity.

apps.v2_14_primary_route: prepared RTDL/OptiX AABB spatial-index query primitive
apps.v4_implication: V4 AABB all-ops/count coverage is bounded operator catalog value, but app-level LibRTS parity is not surprising because V2.14 already had the prepared AABB primitive.
Goal4660/4661 parity is expected: V2.14 already had prepared ranked-summary aggregate. V4 candidate wrappers are not enough for a speed claim.

V4 weighted-sum work is not a clean new app speed win against V2.14 because the serious V2.14 row already used a weighted any-hit sum primitive. The V4/V3 regression must be treated as a blocker, not hidden by the V4/V2 ratio.

goal_level_decision_audit.stupid_action: I was about to select robot_collision mainly from current V4 operator evidence and prior Embree-vs-OptiX evidence without first proving whether V2.14 already had the same primitive route.
goal_level_decision_audit.alternative_path: Audit V2.14 per-app primitives first, then select only targets where V4 has a real new runtime lever or a frozen same-primitive improvement over V2.14.

next_action: Use this audit as a prerequisite for Goal4672 target selection. Robot_collision is demoted from clean next target to same-primitive improvement candidate. If no existing app has a nontrivial V4-new lever, Goal4672 must say that a new generic primitive is required rather than inventing a weak target.
